item.description: A rope access technician had a fatal fall from around 8.5 m while engaged in routine maintenance activities on a pipelay tower

item.title: 22/23: Finger injury while setting up pipe cutting operation
item.description: A crew member was setting up a pipe cutting machine in a vertical position to cut welding that was done on a jumper for repair, when they suffered a finger injury.

item.title: 21/23: Fatality during transfer of pipes
item.description: Lifting operation: A person has been killed during the transfer of pipework between quay and vessel; the incident is still under investigation

item.title: 21/23: Getting fall arrest equipment right
item.description: Despite a permit to work being in place for a crew member to work at height on a vessel, the length of fall arrest equipment was found to be greater than the height at which the crew member was working

item.title: 21/23: Paper shredder – explosion
item.description: Incorrect lubrication of blades in an office paper shredder caused it to explode; the shredder’s plastic bin was destroyed but no-one was harmed

item.title: 21/23: MSF: Air cylinder – high pressure discharge
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has published Safety Alert 23-10 relating to pillar valve failure of a breathing apparatus bottle

item.title: 21/23: BSEE: Improper use and application of high-pressure hoses
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 465 relating to the improper use and application of high-pressure hoses

item.title: 20/23: LTI – Person fractured pelvis in a fall from a ladder
item.description: Onboard a cargo vessel a crew member fell 4-5 metres from a temporary access ladder and fractured his pelvis; after surgery, the injured person needed at least three months to recover

item.title: 20/23: Caught between: Unplanned movement of equipment leads to severe injuries
item.description: A mechanic was caught in the door of a freight container by a tipped-over hose saddle weighing 3 tonnes; he sustained severe injuries that required surgery and was off work for more than 6 months

item.title: 20/23: Unplanned rotation of drilling machinery
item.description: During scheduled maintenance of a large subsea drill, the drill bit started rotating unexpectedly; nobody was nearby at the time and no one was injured

item.title: 20/23: CHIRP: Crew vigilance prevents mooring incident
item.description: The Confidential Human Factors Incident Reporting Programme (CHIRP ) has shared an event in which the careful vigilance of vessel crew prevented a mooring incident

item.title: 20/23: MSF – Two recent dropped object incidents
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety alerts on two recent dropped object incidents, both of which have learning value for IMCA Members

item.title: 19/23: Unexpected descent and ascent of mattress lifting frame
item.description: While concrete mattresses were being moved using a mattress handling frame and the main crane, the frame began moving close to working divers with no intervention from the crane operator

item.title: 19/23: High potential: dropped chain assembly
item.description: A chain assembly weighing 2.3 kg fell 10 m to deck, glancing the helmet of a person working below, but potentially causing fatal injuries

item.title: 19/23: Near miss with high pressure gas due to incorrect procedures
item.description: A crew narrowly avoided potentially serious problems with a high pressure gas supply by stopping and thinking things through

item.title: 19/23: Electrocution incident – make sure electrical equipment is safe!
item.description: A vessel cook received a mains electric shock when he simultaneously touched a metal bain-marie AND the messroom service window with both of his hands

item.title: 19/23: MSF: Person injured falling between decks
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has published Safety Alert 23-06 relating to someone who fell 2 m between decks on an Anchor Handling Tug Supply (AHTS ) vessel alongside in port

item.title: 18/23: Restricted air supply to diver
item.description: During a diver recovery drill, a contracted subsea company encountered significant issues that led to the standby diver momentarily losing his main air supply, which resulted in the diver going on bailout and the drill being aborted

item.title: 18/23: LTI – Crew member fell down open hatch
item.description: During mooring, while attempting to secure the rope on the aft section of the vessel, a crew member stumbled and fell into an open hatchway, suffering three broken ribs, which led to a Lost Time Injury (LTI)

item.title: 18/23: Fire in diesel generator following tests
item.description: In the engine room of a vessel in port, fire broke out in a diesel generator undergoing maintenance by a third-party team; the generator was brought to a stop and the fire was put out

item.title: 18/23: Chain caught and broke
item.description: Crew were removing a hydrogen gland from a generator using a lifting attachment, two chain falls, and an overhead crane. One of the chain fall’s pull chains caught on a bolt on the top of the generator and broke.

item.title: 18/23: BSEE: Overhaul Ball falls to deck resulting in High Potential near miss
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 460 relating to a dropped object during lifting operations

item.title: 17/23: Serious finger injury in power operated watertight sliding door
item.description: A crew person suffered a very serious finger injury in a watertight sliding door when the vessel rolled with the swell.

item.title: 17/23: LTI: Serious hand injury – fingers lost in unexpected hatch closure
item.description: A crew member was badly injured when the engine room’s emergency hatch cover closed unexpectedly on his fingers

item.title: 17/23: Finger injury during lifting operations
item.description: A Second Engineer went to assist crew members with positioning a pallet of cylinders for a lift operation, but got his right hand trapped below one of the cylinders - the middle finger was pinched and injured

item.title: 17/23: Finger injury during shackle handling
item.description: During a pennant wire spooling operation, a crew member was trying to remove a 35 tonne SWL shackle from the pennant eye, but the shackle landed on his left-hand middle finger causing a crush injury 1.5cm long

item.title: 17/23: Hand and finger injuries
item.description: Hand and finger injuries comprise almost a fifth of the incidents and events submitted by IMCA members just in the last year

item.title: 16/23: Crew member in small boat slipped and dislocated shoulder
item.description: A crew member kneeling down in a workboat was injured when the boat moved suddenly as a result of the sea state

item.title: 16/23: Small boat crew exposed to FPSO process water discharge (fumes and aerosol)
item.description: During diving operations on a live FPSO, the deck crew on the Light Dive Craft (LDC) and Fast Rescue Craft (FRC) were exposed to fumes and aerosols from the FPSO process water discharge

item.title: 16/23: LTI – Crew person cracked shin bone
item.description: An engineer suffered a broken shin when he slipped taking a shortcut into the engine room

item.title: 16/23: Person slipped on stairway while wearing shoe covers
item.description: While descending a vessel staircase in safety boots with company-approved shoe covers on, a person slipped down approximately four steps on the staircase. The person had a firm grip on the handrail at the time and thereby prevented further slippage. The strain of preventing a worse fall caused muscular pain on the left side of their torso and their left shoulder.

item.title: 16/23: BSEE: Lack of training with hydraulic torque wrench contributes to fatality
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 459 relating to a fatality which occurred on a drillship in the Gulf of Mexico.

item.title: 15/23: Lifting chains parted – hydrogen embrittlement
item.description: On a vessel involved in project demobilisation, three of four lifting chains on a load parted while the load was being lifted.

item.title: 15/23: Davit hook failures
item.description: A member reports two separate instances where a workboat davit hook, and life raft davit hook components, have failed.

item.title: 15/23: Sheave became detached during lifting operations
item.description: During recovery operations of marine geophysical sensors, a sheave parted from a swivel connection on the A-frame

item.title: 15/23: Near miss: Personnel transfer basket hit structure
item.description: While transferring two personnel to a platform using the vessel crane, the base bumper of the personnel transfer basket came into contact with the helipad netting rail of the platform

item.title: 15/23: BSEE: A warning on tagline entanglement
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 461 relating to recent tagline entanglements which have resulted in several High Potential near misses

item.title: 14/23: MAIB: High pressure oil leak causes a fire in the engine room
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published Safety Digest 1/2023, consisting of lessons from recent Marine Accident Reports. IMCA has reviewed the digest and here passes on for members interest some but not all of the incidents in it.

item.title: 14/23: MAIB: Gantry crane wire parted causing injury
item.description: A gantry crane hoist wire parted causing a load to drop, causing injury and damage to equipment

item.title: 14/23: MAIB: A heavy sheave fell over causing an LTI
item.description: A bosun suffered a broken leg when a heavy sheave he was trying to manoeuvre, fell against him

item.title: 14/23: MAIB: Who is in control?
item.description: Control was lost of a vessel and it almost ran aground. Fortunately, the crew were able to regain control before the vessel (a ferry) grounded, and the voyage continued safely.

item.title: 14/23: MAIB: Lithium-ion battery fire
item.description: Water got into lithium-ion batteries in equipment for use subsea, causing an explosion

item.title: 13/23: Loss of redundancy in diving bell launch and recovery (LARS) PLC system
item.description: During vessel transit to an offshore field, Dive Technicians on a routine walkaround noticed an alarm from the dive bell Launch and Recovery System (LARS). Investigation indicated loss of automatic (LARS) PLC redundancy caused by failure of one of the PLC fibre optic processor synchronisation links. This resulted in the loss of normal operation and increased the risk of single point failure of the LARS.

item.title: 13/23: Hand injury in medical airlock
item.description: A Life Support Technician (LST) suffered a finger injury whilst operating the medical airlock (“Med-lock”) on a dive chamber

item.title: 13/23: Painter line snapped and hit crew member in the face
item.description: A painter line snapped during towing operations; the flying end struck a worker in the face and destroyed his safety glasses.

item.title: 13/23: MSF: Disposable vape self-ignition
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has published Safety Alert 23-03 relating to an incident where an e-cigarette (“vape”) caused a small fire

item.title: 13/23: Hand injury while using manual torque tool
item.description: A Project Engineer injured his hand while using a manual torque wrench with force multiplier attached

item.title: 12/23: Differential pressure: Dummy choke ejected close to divers
item.description: A dummy choke insert was ejected from a water injection (WI) tree by force of differential pressure, while two divers were working nearby; neither diver was in the direct line of fire; both were unharmed

item.title: 12/23: Crane boom stopper fell to main deck
item.description: A knuckle boom stopper pad fell to the main deck directly below the knuckle boom; no personnel were injured - however, there was potential for serious or fatal injury

item.title: 12/23: Fire alarm activation in engine room
item.description: A supply vessel was operating within the 500m safety zone of an offshore platform when fire broke out in the engine room, causing a little damage but no harm to personnel. An alarm activated on the vessel’s fire alarm control panel, indicating a fire in the starboard side engine room cement compartment.

item.title: 12/23: BSEE: Swing rope transfers
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 456 relating to the dangers inherent to swing rope transfers. The BSEE notes that “personnel transfers using swing ropes and baskets present a considerable risk for offshore workers.” The use of swing ropes is not permitted in some parts of the world.

item.title: 12/23: Close approach of AHTS vessel to offshore rig
item.description: During anchor handling operations for an offshore rig, the stern of an Anchor Handling Tug Supply (AHTS) vessel was pulled to starboard, resulting in a bow side close approach to a mooring line

item.title: 11/23: Uncontrolled movement of spreader bar
item.description: A vessel was set up alongside a barge in preparation for the subsea deployment of a 16″ (40cm) spool. The spreader bar sea-fastenings were removed by the deck crew and as the crane raised the rigging, the spreader bar rotated uncontrollably causing it to fall from its supports, with the forward end landing on deck and aft end landing on the spool

item.title: 11/23: Inspection notice from Crosby on certain products
item.description: The Crosby Group has asked IMCA to circulate the following information as part of a Safety Flash

item.title: 11/23: Equipment starts unexpectedly
item.description: A high-voltage AC unit was locked out / tagged out for routine maintenance by three mechanics, but started up unexpectedly

item.title: 11/23: Near Miss: Steam and water released from filter
item.description: Steam and water were unexpectedly released from a filter when a mechanic was cleaning out strainers from a boiler circulation pump

item.title: 11/23: Maintenance and control of fire doors
item.description: A Member has discovered instances of mandatory fire doors onboard their vessels being in a poor state of maintenance, and in some cases modified to alter the closing mechanism or tied back to prevent closing

item.title: 10/23: BSEE: Person injured when safety mechanisms failed
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 455 relating to an incident in which a third-party contract operator sandblasting offshore was injured when a temporary air dryer used for sandblasting operations recoiled and broke the safety cable.

item.title: 10/23: Dropped spanner falls 15 m
item.description: During work at height, a spanner became disconnected from its DROPS protection lanyard whilst crew were working in an area outside the installed protective netting. The spanner then fell to deck 15 metres below.

item.title: 10/23: Equipment damage: Dropped object from tiltable lay system
item.description: During function testing of a tensioner on a pipelay system, a bracket weighing 10.5 kg fell 16 m to deck. The tensioner doors had to be moved into the firing line, closed, and then retracted to the parked position.

item.title: 10/23: Near Miss: Personnel nearly struck by rotating chain attached to flexible pipe
item.description: During a transfer of the second end of a 4" (10 cm) production flexible, the production flexible began rotating due to residual torsion that had built up within the line. A 16.5te chain attached to the pull-in head also began spinning. Two nearby crew members who were observing the operation were almost struck by the spinning chain.

item.title: 10/23: Near miss – Messroom fridge fell over during rough seas
item.description: During transit through heavy seas, a fridge tore loose from the messroom wall and fell on its side.

item.title: 09/23: LTI finger injury during mooring operations
item.description: An AB got his left index finger trapped between a bitt and a mooring rope, resulting in a broken finger and 45 days off work. The incident occurred during un-mooring at the end of a ship-to-ship refuelling operation.

item.title: 09/23: Crew member trapped his left index finger in watertight door
item.description: A visual alarm on the bridge indicated that a watertight door near one of the engine rooms was open. Following this, during testing of the watertight door, a fitter’s left index finger was pinched between the moving door edge and door frame, causing small abrasions to the index finger.

item.title: 09/23: Hand injury from portable grinder
item.description: During flowline fabrication work at a spool base, a subcontract worker received a 3cm laceration to the hand while using a portable grinder

item.title: 09/23: Cut and bruise to right hand whilst pressure testing
item.description: A technician was pressure testing hydraulic hoses when a release of pressure occurred, knocking his hand onto the wall of the test kit, resulting in a laceration to the palm and a bruise to the back of his right hand.

item.title: 09/23: LTI: Hand injury in galley
item.description: In a vessel alongside at Christmas, the cook was preparing meat when his knife slipped and jabbed the top left part of the palm of his left hand, causing a serious laceration

item.title: 08/23: Serious LTI – Crew member slipped on deck breaking his leg
item.description: Three engineering crew members were involved in the manual handling of a bunker hose from an upper storage area to a lower deck storage area accessed via a spiral staircase. One of the engineers slipped on a greasy area of the deck breaking his right leg (fibula or calf bone) in the fall.

item.title: 08/23: Head injury when crew member fell over in bathroom during heavy weather
item.description: A vessel crew member lost balance, tripped and hit his head against the towel rail in his cabin bathroom while the vessel was rolling violently; five stitches were required to close the wound

item.title: 08/23: Person slipped when exiting bathroom into cabin
item.description: A crew member stepped out of the bathroom onto the cabin mat, when the mat slipped resulting in the crew member falling backwards, striking his lower back on the base of the bathroom door frame.

item.title: 08/23: Leak of oil-based mud
item.description: A vessel was preparing to transfer oil-based mud to the shore base. The shore base team began pressure testing their hose to ensure there was no leakage, but during the test about 20-25 litres of mud came out of the tank ventilation.

item.title: 08/23: Life raft secured incorrectly on cradle
item.description: During an onshore visit to a vessel, a life raft was observed to be attached/connected incorrectly to the life raft cradle. The life raft painter rope was connected to the cradle instead of to the weak link on the Hydrostatic Release Unit.

item.title: 07/23: Lift bag near miss
item.description: During the over-boarding of a spool, a lift bag while being inflated, ascended through the engineered rigging arrangement and was caught by the contingency rigging. Our Member considered this incident to have had the potential for a serious injury or fatality.

item.title: 07/23: Finger crushed under Tether Management System (TMS) protection guard
item.description: A worker suffered a crushed finger when the protection guard of a Saab Seaeye TMS8 Tether Management System fell on their finger. The worker was closing and securing the protection guard and lost grip on the guard.

item.title: 07/23: Sudden and uncontrollable move of A&R head
item.description: Abandonment and Recovery (A&R) head was being prepared for welding at the end of offshore pipeline installation operations. As final adjustments were being made, the A&R head assembly was moved upwards and then ejected in an uncontrolled manner from the pipe end.

item.title: 06/23: Ineffective Crane Stinger Hook Pin Installation (BSEE)
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Report 452 relating to a high-potential dropped object incident on a Gulf of Mexico energy facility

item.title: 06/23: Poor control of work in dry dock
item.description: A member reports several cases of hot work and other activities being conducted by contractors on a vessel hull during dry dock/maintenance activities, in which the work was not fully or appropriately under the control of vessel management

item.title: 06/23: Battery explosion during routine maintenance
item.description: A Chief Engineer suffered minor injuries in a battery explosion when disconnecting a cable from the battery; the incident occurred onboard a harbour tug

item.title: 06/23: Near miss: Foreign body in diver’s helmet, resulting in fall of gas pressure
item.description: During a routine dive at a depth of 18 m (60’), the diver reported to the Dive Supervisor a drop in breathing gas pressure; on returning to the vessel and removing the helmet, a foreign body was found in the demand valve chamber section of the helmet regulator

item.title: 06/23: Compressor fire
item.description: Fire broke out in in a 25bar high flow diesel-driven screw compressor installed on the back deck of a diving support vessel operating within the 500m zone of an offshore platform

item.title: 05/23: LTI: Person crushed in watertight door
item.description: An electrician was crushed and severely injured while working on a watertight door on a vessel.

item.title: 05/23: LTI: Finger crushed while moving mobile gantry crane
item.description: A crew member suffered a crushed index finger during manual handling of heavy equipment.

item.title: 05/23: LTI: Crew member crushed finger when opening fire flap
item.description: A crew member injured his finger while opening an emergency fire flap. The incident occurred after an annual test of the deluge system during which the emergency fire flaps had to be closed.

item.title: 05/23: High potential incident: Person struck by Yokohama fender
item.description: While a Yokohama fender was being lifted onboard a vessel in harbour, a crewman came within the line of fire between the fender and bumper bars protecting an electrical services panel; he was struck and injured as the fender moved

item.title: 05/23: LTI: Carbon Monoxide (CO) poisoning during Oxy-Acetylene brazing
item.description: Crew member was repairing a broken valve, part of the Freon pipe system for refrigeration

item.title: 04/23: Uncertified lifting gear found in use
item.description: A number of shackles and other lifting equipment were observed in use onboard a vessel with no certification or inspection reports available

item.title: 04/23: High-potential near miss: Uncontrollable movement of auxiliary whip line
item.description: Crane's block and hook were ejected forward until they hit a stair railing, approx. 4 m forward of the sheave; they then fell approx. 3 m to the deck, and bounced before coming to rest

item.title: 04/23: Dropped objects in dry dock
item.description: A member reports two dropped object incidents during a vessel dry-dock, both with serious injury potential.

item.title: 04/23: Air hose connection failure
item.description: An air supply hose on an air-driven tugger winch snapped out under pressure from the cam lock adapter.

item.title: 04/23: Electrolytic corrosion: Failure of fire hose couplings
item.description: Electrolytic corrosion: Failure of fire hose couplings

item.title: 03/23: Diving instructor killed - incorrect valve threads
item.description: During a dive, the valve came loose from the diving cylinder and fatally hit the diving instructor

item.title: 03/23: Near miss: pilot ladder – side rope failed
item.description: Whilst undertaking pilot boarding operations during the hours of darkness, a side rope on the pilot ladder parted while being weight tested by the pilot.

item.title: 03/23: LTI - Finger injury during davit test
item.description: LTI - Finger injury during davit test

item.title: 03/23: Small fire following hot work
item.description: On a Member’s vessel alongside, a small fire started following hot work conducted by the client’s welding sub-contractors.

item.title: 03/23: Single point failure resulting in a dropped object
item.description: A small part weighing 0.3 kg fell 20 metres from an OMC-160 wind speed and direction sensor installed on a vessel’s main mast

item.title: 02/23: Umbilical management – near miss
item.description: Diver discovered that his umbilical was trapped and was able to free it himself.

item.title: 02/23: Lost ROV incident
item.description: A number of incidents have been reported where loads have been dropped during subsea operations.

item.title: 02/23: Blocked emergency exit hatch
item.description: An engine room emergency exit hatch could not be opened

item.title: 02/23: Serious hand injury (MSF)
item.description: Serious hand injury during mooring operations

item.title: 02/23: Incorrect gangway rigging
item.description: A member reports several cases of gangways being rigged incorrectly.

item.title: 22/22 Diver Finger Injury – Scrubber Blower Fan
item.description: A diver suffered a minor hand injury when he put his hand on part of a fan which should not have been exposed.

item.title: 22/22 BSEE: Unsecured Pressurised Hoses Result in Hand Injuries
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement BSEE) has published Safety Alert No. 442 relating to hand injuries caused by handling unsecured pressurised hoses during coil tubing operations.

item.title: 22/22 Cook’s arm scalded while removing food from oven
item.description: Whilst removing a tray, scalding hot water (condensed steam) on the surface of the lid dripped onto cook’s arm.

item.title: 22/22 LTI: fractured finger during anchor handling
item.description: A crew member suffered a serious finger injury when he got his finger trapped.

item.title: 22/22 LTI: person struck by uncontrolled swing in chain
item.description: An anchor chain swung unexpectedly across the deck and hit a crew member, causing an injury to his foot resulting in an LTRI.

item.title: 21/22 BSEE – “Green hats” – training and supervision of short service employees
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement has published Safety Alert #440.

item.title: 21/22 American P&I Club: Vessel grounding – fatigue was a factor
item.description: The American P&I Club, as part of its “Good Catch” safety series, has published a bulletin relating to a towing vessel grounding in which fatigue was a factor.

item.title: 21/22 MAIB: Capsize and sinking of fishing vessel Joanna C – vessel stability
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published Accident Investigation Report 7/2022 into the capsize and sinking with loss of life, of the fishing vessel Joanna C.

item.title: 20/22 LTI: Diver suffered crush injury to finger
item.description: A diver sustained a crush injury to his finger.

item.title: 20/22 High potential incident – Foot trapped under ram cylinder
item.description: A person almost had his foot crushed by a ram cylinder on a pipeline coating machine.

item.title: 20/22 Fall leading to serious personal injury
item.description: A crew member suffered a fall leading to concussion and other serious injuries.

item.title: 20/22 Chemical burns to body
item.description: CHIRP Maritime, an industry charity facilitating confidential incident reporting from seafarers, has published its Annual Digest 2021.

item.title: 20/22 Personal injury – burns from hot engine oil to body and face
item.description: CHIRP Maritime, an industry charity facilitating confidential incident reporting from seafarers, has published its Annual Digest 2021.

item.title: 19/22 Third-party truck not in appropriate or safe condition
item.description: Trucks to be used for the pipes were inspected and several defects identified.

item.title: 19/22 Machinery breakdown leads to a collision
item.description: CHIRP Maritime, an industry charity facilitating confidential incident reporting from seafarers, has published its Annual Digest 2021.

item.title: 19/22 Equipment found live: drawings incorrect for Lock-out/Tag-out
item.description: During an inspection, it was discovered that the heaters were still live and energized.

item.title: 19/22 MSF: CO2 system left non-operational after servicing
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published Safety Alert 22-10 relating to an important safety system being left non-operational after it was serviced.

item.title: 19/22 Accidental release of free-fall lifeboat
item.description: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada (TSB) has published Safety investigation report M20P0353 relating to the accidental release of a free-fall lifeboat from a bulk carrier.

item.title: 18/22 Flash fire on Oxygen gas quad hose

item.description: The Marine Safety Forum have published Safety Alert 21-12 relating to a person who was injured as a result of being suspended in a safety harness during a rescue at height drill.

item.title: 22/21: Wear a life-jacket!! (MAIB)
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published an instructive and useful account of a recent man overboard exercise, which is summarised below for Members

item.title: 21/21: COBRA bailout system – guidance note
item.description: JFD has issued a COBRA guidance note relating to concerns regarding the suitability of the 2L composite cylinders contained within the set. This note highlights to users, those reported concerns and the follow-on investigation that has been undertaken to demonstrate suitability of the composite cylinders for the application in COBRA.

item.title: 21/21: Acetylene quad fire on quayside
item.description: A Member reports an acetylene gas quad fire which occurred on the quayside. No injuries occurred during the event.

item.title: 21/21: Descending stairs safely
item.description: On one of our members’ vessels, an observation was raised relating to the hazards associated with steep stairs.

item.title: 21/21: MAIB: Grounding of general cargo vessel Kaami
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published Accident Investigation Report 7/2021 into the running aground of a cargo vessel in March 2020

item.title: 21/21: Fault in high voltage equipment
item.description: A serious fault was discovered in high voltage (-5600 V) equipment; the fault caused sparks to be observed across the high voltage terminals

item.title: 20/21: Failure of dive chamber overhead door centre pin
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has published Safety Alert 21-10 relating to a crew member who suffered an unpleasant cut to the hand whilst engaged in routine cleaning.

item.title: 20/21: HSE: Catastrophic failure of marine loading arm
item.description: The UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) has published a safety alert on the catastrophic failure of a marine loading arm. Marine loading arms (MLAs) are used to transfer material from ship to shore. Full alert found here.

item.title: 20/21: WSH: Two workers passed out and died in a dredger's ballast tank
item.description: The Workplace Safety and Health Council of Singapore (WSH) reported in Accident Notification of 24 May 2021, that two workers had passed out and died in a dredger’s ballast tank.

item.title: 20/21: MAIB: fatality during transfer from a workboat to a barge
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published Accident Investigation Report 6/2021 into the death of a crewman whilst transferring between the workboat Beinn Na Caillich and a barge at a fish farm

item.title: 20/21: HSE: Allergic reaction at work
item.description: The UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) have fined a company over £100,000 after an employee developed an allergic form of dermatitis after coming into contact with metalworking fluids. See here for press release.

item.title: 19/21: Overheated transformer activated fire alarm
item.description: An under-rated transformer was installed, causing overheating and thermal degradation of the transformer which subsequently tripped the breaker and activated the vessel’s fire alarm

item.title: 19/21: Mains extension melted – not fully paid out
item.description: Mains extension melted – not fully paid out

item.title: 19/21: Catering crew unfamiliar with firefighting systems and emergency stops
item.description: During a recent incident on a members’ vessel, the catering crew were found to be unfamiliar with the firefighting systems and electrical equipment emergency stops

item.title: 19/21: Incidents relating to hatches and doors
item.description: A Member reports a number of incidents relating to hatches and doors, which can be summarised briefly for our instruction here

item.title: 19/21: MSF: Cut Hand Whilst Cleaning / Hand Safety
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has published Safety Alert 21-10 relating to a crew member who suffered an unpleasant cut to the hand whilst engaged in routine cleaning.

item.title: 17/21: Lifting frame detached from fast rescue craft (FRC)
item.description: IMCA has received information relating to an incident in which a lifting frame became detached from a fast rescue craft (FRC) during operations

item.title: 17/21: Failure of EGS valve stem on dive helmet
item.description: A member reported an incident in which the emergency gas system (EGS) valve handle on a commercial diving helmet broke off. At the time of the failure the dive helmet was undergoing pre-dive inspection on deck.

item.title: 17/21: Dropped object during lifting operations
item.description: A part weighing 8.5 kg fell over 15 m from a pipelay tower to deck

item.title: 17/21: MSF: Potential dropped object

item.description: During offshore installation activities a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) and Tether Management System (TMS) recovered to deck was observed to have a TMS door missing

item.title: 16/21: Fatality – explosive failure of corroded fire extinguisher
item.description: A person was killed when there was a catastrophic explosive failure of a corroded fire extinguisher

item.title: 16/21: MSF: Tank corrosion
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published Safety Alert 21-07 relating to the discovery of a leak in a tank caused by corrosion.

item.title: 16/21: NTSB: Fire on laid up Dive Support Vessel
item.description: The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) of the USA has published report MAB 21/11 into a fire on board a DSV which was laid up alongside

item.title: 16/21: Inadvertently drinking hazardous substances
item.description: Someone unintentionally drank a hazardous substance out of a drinking water bottle.

item.title: 16/21: MSF: Engine damage after routine maintenance
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has published Safety Alert 21-09 relating to engine damage following routine maintenance.

item.title: 15/21: LTI: Hand injury during diving operations
item.description: A member reports a serious hand injury suffered by a diver working in the water on floating hoses at an SPM (single point mooring).

item.title: 15/21: Learning outcomes from a real time diver recovery
item.description: During a saturation diving operation a dive team became involved in the recovery of an incapacitated diver into their bell.

item.title: 15/21: UK HSE: Employee in a port suffers life changing injuries in clamp truck incident
item.description: The UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) fined a port following an incident in which an employee was seriously injured by a clamp truck. [Similar to a forklift, but instead of forks, a clamp truck has a hydraulic clamp attachment for handling rolls of paper.]

item.title: 15/21: Inhalation of toxic fumes during hot work
item.description: Two crew members were exposed to toxic fumes resulting in dizziness, headaches, difficulty in breathing, and low blood oxygen levels

item.title: 15/21: UK HSE: Worker fatally injured in oil drum explosion
item.description: The UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) prosecuted a company after a worker was killed when an oil drum exploded during hot work

item.title: 14/21: Floodlight dropped to deck – corrosion
item.description: A floodlight weighing about 6 kg was found on the deck, near to the scaffolding storage area, underneath the main crane boom rest

item.title: 14/21: MAIB: Anchor failures
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published Safety Bulletin 1/2021 relating to anchor failures

item.title: 14/21: Injuries sustained during maintenance – worker positioning
item.description: A member has noted several injuries in the last 6-8 months relating to worker positioning and the use of tools and equipment. A review of these incidents has established a need for improved risk assessments which consider the relationship between the worker, their environment, tools, and activity. We call this the ergonomics of the task.

item.title: 14/21: Britannia P&I Club: Double fatality resulting from confined space entry
item.description: The Britannia P&I Club, as part of their BSAFE campaign have published a case study into a double fatality resulting from confined or enclosed space entry.

item.title: 14/21: Crew member thrown to the quay by unplanned movement of small boat
item.description: The Britannia P&I Club, as part of their BSAFE campaign have published a case study into a double fatality resulting from confined or enclosed space entry.

item.title: 13/21: UK MAIB: Safety Digest – lessons from marine accident reports 1/2021
item.description: The United Kingdom Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published its Safety Digest 1/2021 “which draws the attention of the marine community to some of the lessons arising from investigations into recent accidents and incidents. It contains information which has been determined up to the time of issue.”

item.title: 13/21: CHIRP Maritime – Annual digest for 2020
item.description: CHIRP stands for Confidential Human Factors Incident Reporting Programme. One of the aims of CHIRP is to contribute to the enhancement of maritime safety worldwide, by providing a totally independent confidential (not anonymous) reporting system for all individuals employed in or associated with these industries.

item.title: 13/21: Leg injury when struck by rebounding hammer
item.description: A crew member was struck on the right lower leg (the shin) by a rebounding hammer. The incident occurred when he was using the hammer to remove a stainless steel securing pin on the brake band drum of a tugger winch.

item.title: 13/21: Swedish Club: Lessons learned – crew member loses leg in mooring injury
item.description: The Swedish [P&I] Club has recently released a “casebook” containing safety lessons learned from maritime incidents. This useful resource document can be found here: www.swedishclub.com/loss-prevention/cases/case-studies/. One of the case studies describes a very serious injury of a crew member during mooring operations.

item.title: 13/21: Two injuries
item.description: A Member reports two injuries during operations, highlighting the need for continued vigilance and care in everyday activities.

item.title: 12/21: Update to SF 08/21: fatality – person crushed when secured material fell on him
item.description: This is an updated version of the event published in SF 08/21, wherein stored metal plates fell on a crewman causing fatal injuries. It was originally shared with one of our members by a client company, and was public domain news. It does not involve an IMCA member. This updated version has been shared by the company involved.

item.title: 12/21: Only a centimetre – an emergency exit hatch blocked by mooring ropes
item.description: On a vessel alongside in port, an emergency exit hatch was found to be blocked. A team making a daily inspection tour round the vessel found that they could not open an emergency exit hatch providing egress from the engine room to deck on the port side at the stern.

item.title: 12/21: Potential dropped object from container
item.description: Before backloading a container from rig to vessel, it was noted that there were two metal blocks in the top corner pockets of the container.

item.title: 12/21: MSF: Wearing and storage of eye protection
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published Safety Alert 21-05 relating to a recent incident involving safety equipment and its storage.

item.title: 12/21: Malaria hasn’t gone away
item.description: A Member reports that in February 2021 one of their personnel had been admitted to the Intensive Care Unit of their local hospital, with confirmed malaria

item.title: 11/21: MAIB: Engine failure and subsequent fire
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch has published it’s report 2/2021 into an engine failure and subsequent fire on ro-ro cargo vessel Finlandia Seaways in April 2018.

item.title: 11/21: BSEE: Crewman fell to his death through faulty grating
item.description: The United States’ Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published BSEE Panel Report 2021-001 into a fatal fall from a platform in the Gulf of Mexico in 2019

item.title: 11/21: Mooring: Increase in first aid cases involving over-exertion
item.description: A member has noted that in recent months, there have been several accidents related to over-exertion. Most of these incidents have involved mooring operations, a job that requires physical effort due to the handling of heavy lines.

item.title: 11/21: Hand injury from falling object during lifting operations
item.description: A member has noted that in recent months, there have been several accidents related to over-exertion. Most of these incidents have involved mooring operations, a job that requires physical effort due to the handling of heavy lines.

item.title: 11/21: Life raft dropped to the jetty
item.description: A member has noted that in recent months, there have been several accidents related to over-exertion. Most of these incidents have involved mooring operations, a job that requires physical effort due to the handling of heavy lines.

item.title: 10/21: Near miss: vessel approach to wind turbine tower
item.description: A Member reports two near miss incidents within two weeks of one another, in which during the approach of a vessel to a wind turbine tower, the nacelle started moving, with the risk of the vessel being hit or gangway being knocked off by the wind turbine blades.

item.title: 10/21: Dropped 0bject – Crane auxiliary block dropped from crane boom
item.description: Two sub-contracted crane technicians were mobilised to the vessel to inspect the pipelay system 15Te crane before a load and rock test of the crane took place.

item.title: 10/21: Shipyard worker receives electrical shock
item.description: A shipyard worker received a serious electrical shock onboard a vessel in dry dock. The incident occurred when a shipyard welding team were setting up equipment outside on the main deck.

item.title: 10/21: SIMOPS – Smoke from hot work task enters confined space
item.description: A portable fan providing fresh air to a tank cleaning operation (requiring confined space entry permit), began drawing in smoke from an oxy-propane cutting operation nearby; the workers inside the confined space were instructed to vacate the tank immediately; no-one was harmed

item.title: 10/21: LTI during deck cargo operations
item.description: A crew member was seriously injured while pipe bundles were being lifted by crane from the vessel onto a fixed structure

item.title: 09/21: Dropped object during crane operations
item.description: A piece of timber weighing 7.6 kg fell approximately 10 m from a crane jib and landed on the main deck

item.title: 09/21: Dropped object – Steel deck plate falls from pipelay tower
item.description: During testing and inspection of the pipelay tower on a vessel in dry dock, a large steel deck plate fell 9 m from the tower to deck

item.title: 09/21: Incorrect measurement and markings on divers umbilical
item.description: During a diving operation it was seen that the colour distance markings on the divers umbilical were not the same as stated in the diving contractor’s Diving Operations Manual

item.title: 09/21: Case study: Lone watchkeeping grounding at night
item.description: A vessel ran aground at night after the Officer of the Watch failed to effectively monitor the ship’s progress for about two hours

item.title: 09/21: Engineer suffered burn injuries in engine room incident
item.description: The Belgian Federal Bureau for the Investigation of Maritime Accidents (FEBIMA) has published its detailed and informative Report 2020/003688 “Report on the investigation into a serious injury on board” the capesize bulk carrier Mineral Temse in May 2020.

item.title: 08/21: Fatality: Person crushed when secured material fell on him
item.description: In two separate incidents at Great Yarmouth in the UK, two vessels have sustained damage to hull plating and hull fenders through contact with damaged, missing or misaligned jetty fendering arrangements.

item.title: 08/21: Crane wire parted during offshore operations
item.description: A concrete mattress was being deployed as part of the construction of a pipeline crossing. As the load was swung outboard and before it entered the water, the crane wire parted causing the load to fall to the seabed.

item.title: 08/21: Tumble dryer fire: lint ignition

item.title: 08/21: Electric shock due to water in electrical equipment
item.description: There was an uncontrolled spraying of fresh water from a sounding pipe in the galley, resulting in electrical equipment getting wet. As a result someone got an electric shock.

item.title: 08/21: MSF: Air cylinder failure in lifeboat

item.title: 29/20: Crushed finger injury during wire transfer operations
item.description: The crew used a crowbar to try and free the stopper chain from the wire. This was done by inserting the crowbar underneath the wire to lift it up from the deck. One of the ABs was removing the stopper chain whilst the crow bar held it up. However, the crowbar was removed too early resulting in the wire falling to the deck whilst his hand was still underneath it. This resulted in a crush injury to the left index finger.

item.description: High potential DROPS near miss: Failed crane component

item.title: 26/20: Near miss: Lever hoist failure
item.description: A lever hoist failed causing a load to descend to deck in an uncontrolled manner. The near miss incident occurred when a set of 1m trenching swords were being lowered to deck. The lever hoist being used was rated to 1.6Te, more than capable of lifting the load which was approximately 200kg in weight.

item.title: 26/20: Provisions crane damaged by main deck crane
item.description: During vessel mobilization the boat cradle had to be shifted from centre of the main deck towards the starboard side closer to the accommodation. The Main Crane was used for this lift and the Provisions Crane was parked in standby facing aft. While slewing the Main Crane to starboard, the Main Crane jib crane came into contact with the jib on the Provisions Crane. The Provisions crane was inspected after impact and mechanical damage was found on the slewing gear and pinion gear.

item.title: 26/20: Dropped Object from Derrick
item.description: During vessel mobilization the boat cradle had to be shifted from centre of the main deck towards the starboard side closer to the accommodation. The Main Crane was used for this lift and the Provisions Crane was parked in standby facing aft. While slewing the Main Crane to starboard, the Main Crane jib crane came into contact with the jib on the Provisions Crane. The Provisions crane was inspected after impact and mechanical damage was found on the slewing gear and pinion gear.

item.title: 26/20: Fall of a suspended load on general cargo vessel ZEA Servant injuring two crew
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published an Accident Investigation Report 11/2020 relating to an incident on the general cargo vessel ZEA Servant in Campbeltown, Scotland. Two crewmen were injured when a suspended load fell and struck them.

item.title: 25/20: Emergency Lithium battery failed catastrophically in a diving bell
item.description: Emergency Lithium battery failed catastrophically in a diving bell

item.title: 25/20: Fire in welding fumes extraction system
item.description: Fire in welding fumes extraction system

item.title: 25/20: High potential near miss: Nitrogen hose failure during transfer of gas
item.description: A supply hose had detached from its ferrule and approximately 165,000 litres of pure nitrogen was released into the room. Consequently this reduced the oxygen levels in the room to approximately 17.4% (normal oxygen content in the atmosphere is 20.8%).

item.title: 25/20: Electrical shock from containerised portable office
item.description: Whilst tidying a mobile office (freight) container, an employee sustained a mild electric shock by inadvertently touching an exposed live electrical cable which was obscured by several boxes below a desk

item.title: 25/20: Unsafe use of hand grinder with damaged disc
item.description: Grinding machine was observed as used with damaged grinding disc. Broken disc projectile could potentially cause serious injuries. Many other workers have been injured when angle grinders have kicked back, causing cuts and lacerations.

item.title: 24/20: Hull damage caused oil leakage from settling tank
item.description: On a member’s vessel, the starboard forward Marine Gas Oil (MGO) settling tank was punctured during berthing operations

item.title: 24/20: Safe embarkation and disembarkation of Marine Pilots
item.description: During the embarkation of the Pilot to the vessel, the Pilot observed that a step on the Pilot ladder was not in good condition (broken). The Pilot implemented the Stop Work Policy and informed the Master of the vessel, noting that the Pilot ladder would need changing before he would embark.

item.title: 24/20: Near miss: Incorrectly set lifeboat hook
item.description: During a routine launch and recovery drill, the lifeboat crew became concerned that the forward hook was not engaging correctly despite the ‘padlock’ symbol indicating correct closure.

item.title: 24/20: Positive: STOP WORK by Master challenging Sailing Order
item.description: During a routine launch and recovery drill, the lifeboat crew became concerned that the forward hook was not engaging correctly despite the ‘padlock’ symbol indicating correct closure.

item.title: 24/20: Near miss/positive: Internal O-ring seal found damaged on fuel system
item.description: In a vessel alongside, a new fuel gas cylinder was connected to a gas-powered forklift truck. When the delivery valve was opened gas leaked from the connection between the cylinder and the hose. The cylinder was removed and the internal O-ring seal was found to be damaged.

item.title: 23/20: Safety performance in the offshore renewable energy industry
item.description: The UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) has written to a number of trade bodies representing the offshore renewable energy industry, including IMCA, expressing concern “that in some sectors of the wind energy industry, improvements in health and safety performance has at best stalled if not reversed. In 2020, there have been a number of serious incidents both in the UK and elsewhere which could indicate that any reversal may continue.”

item.title: 23/20: Use of face masks designated KN95
item.description: The UK HSE (Health and Safety Executive) has issued the following notice regarding the use of face masks designated KN95

item.title: 22/20: Finger injury caused by incorrectly secured console cover
item.description: An incorrectly secured console cover closed in an unplanned and unexpected way, trapping a crew member’s finger, which was injured

item.title: 22/20: Hydraulic sample extruder – finger laceration
item.description: Whilst using a hydraulic sample extruder in a laboratory, the technician caught and injured his finger between the Shelby tube and extruder ram while trying to stabilise the dolly

item.title: 22/20: LTI: Loss of fingertip and nail
item.description: While crew were moving lashing materials (chains, shackles and turnbuckles) from the garage deck into a storage space, the bosun suffered a serious finger injury.

item.title: 22/20: Person injured when leg slipped through floor hatch
item.description: During routine inspection of an engine room, someone slipped through a loose floor hatch plate and sustained a cut wound about 3 cm on the shin of his left leg.

item.title: 22/20: Member of the public was killed following unplanned movement of an unsecured load
item.description: The UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) fined a company after it caused the death of a child when he was trapped between an unsecured pole and a fence.

item.title: 22/20: Cargo Ignited on Truck Bed During Transportation
item.description: There was a fire in the cargo on the back of a truck whilst moving materials from the warehouse to the vessel. Whilst in transit, the driver observed flames coming from the truck bed. He stopped the vehicle and used the vehicle fire extinguisher to tackle the fire. He was successful, despite very strong winds, and then returned to the warehouse safely. No injuries to personnel, no damage to truck.

item.title: 21/20: Double man overboard resulting in one fatality
item.description: During preparations for disconnecting a tow tug which was moored to a barge in turn moored to the jetty, a crew member of the tow tug fell into water between the tow tug and the barge. A second crew member also fell into the water during attempts to rescue his colleague.

item.title: 21/20: MOB fatality from multi-cat
item.description: A Member reports a man overboard fatality which occurred from a multi-cat engaged in shallow water construction in an inshore environment

item.title: 21/20: MOB fatality: Person fell between vessel and jetty
item.description: The Master of dredging vessel Cherry Sand died when he was crushed between the dredger and the jetty after he fell while attempting to step ashore to assist berthing the vessel in Rosyth, Scotland

item.title: 21/20: And finishing on a positive note: A CPR success story – “we saved a life that day”
item.description: The positive outcome of this story, saving a life, is the result of leadership, commitment, and preparedness for the unexpected.

item.title: 20/20: Leg entanglement from Tag Line during cargo operations
item.description: An AB got his leg entangled with a tag line during lifting operations, while a vessel was alongside a rig offloading cargo

item.title: 20/20: High potential incident: gantry hoist failure
item.description: An AB got his leg entangled with a tag line during lifting operations, while a vessel was alongside a rig offloading cargo

item.title: 20/20: Safe use of Flexible Intermediate Bulk Container (FIBC )
item.description: An FIBC was raised to 3–5 metres when a distinctive tearing / ripping sound was heard, it was then the FIBC handle and stitching tore and 900 kg of sand bags fell to the quayside

item.title: 20/20: MSF: Potential dropped objects – nets or tarps to cover cargo?
item.description: Marine Safety Forum Safety Alert 20-04 describes a potential dropped object (PDO) during cargo operations. A wooden baton of the type often used to support covers attached to open topped Cargo Carrying Units (CCUs), was discovered jammed against the underside of a cargo basket.

item.title: 20/20: Manhole opened and not correctly closed
item.description: During a safety round on deck prior to cargo operations it was noticed that a manhole had been opened in order to pump out ballast water to replace a faulty valve.

item.title: 19/20: Fall from a height into a ballast tank
item.description: A worker inside a ballast tank fell from height

item.title: 19/20: Trip and fall down hotel stairs causing serious wrist injury
item.description: Whilst engaged in business travel, an employee of one of our members slipped and fell when descending a hotel staircase

item.title: 19/20: Man overboard from stinger
item.description: A member of the crew fell overboard through an opening in the stinger

item.title: 19/20: USCG: Automatic identification system (AIS) inaccuracies led to fatalities
item.description: The United States Coastguard (USCG) has published Safety Alert 04-20 relating to an incident where a causal factor in a number of fatalities was incorrect information entered into vessel AIS (Automatic Identification Systems). Accurate AIS data entry and display is essential to safe navigation.

item.title: 19/20: Crewman fatally injured while standing on the stern ramp of Seatruck Progress
item.description: Third Officer of the vessel Seatruck Progress was struck and fatally injured by a freight vehicle semi-trailer while standing on the vessel’s stern ramp

item.title: 18/20: Serious injury caused by high-pressure washer
item.description: A work team supervisor sustained a laceration to his upper right thigh caused by a high-pressure water jet

item.title: 18/20: MSF: Water-based mud spill on deck
item.description: During routine mud transfer operations at an offshore installation the rig hose parted from the vessel’s manifold resulting in a release of approximately 2,500 litres of mud to the deck

item.title: 18/20: Lifting basket with unsecured cargo which fell out
item.description: A cargo basket containing equipment was to be lifted from the vessel deck to an offshore installation. The crane on the offshore installation was unable to lift the load, resulting in the basket dropping back to deck and some of the equipment sliding out the basket onto the vessel deck.

item.title: 18/20: Near miss/positive: Crew exercised stop work on new gangway
item.description: A newly installed gangway was found inadequate and unsafe.

item.title: 18/20: Serious incidents involving the weather
item.description: Serious incidents involving the weather

item.title: 17/20: Inadvertent activation of condensed aerosol fire extinguishing system leads to a fatality
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has issued Safety Bulletin SB1/2020 highlighting a potentially serious hazard, associated with condensed aerosol firefighting suppressant particles after a fatal accident on fishing vessel Resurgam

item.title: 17/20: Engine room fire – a small rag left after maintenance
item.description: There was a small fire in the engine room of a large multi-engined vessel

item.title: 17/20: Fire in the engine room
item.description: A vessel suffered a fire in the engine room

item.title: 17/20: UK HSE: Workers injured by unplanned release of mud slurry
item.description: An electricity power station company was prosecuted after three contractors were injured by a sudden release of water and sludge, while carrying out maintenance work

item.title: 16/20: Fall from Height Leading to Injury
item.description: During work to change a wire on an FRC davit, a crewman lost his footing, slipped and fell 2.5m to deck below

item.title: 16/20: Sewage spilled onto the quayside
item.description: 30-40 litres of sewage water was spilled onto the quayside during a transfer operation from vessel to sewage truck. There was no discharge into the sea due to a contained concreted area on the quayside.

item.title: 16/20: Fall from the quayside into water
item.description: Whilst slinging a palleted water bag (load), a third-party contract worker who was assisting in the operation fell approximately 3 metres from the quayside into the water

item.title: 16/20: Pedestal Drill Chuck Assembly Detached Causing Head Injury
item.description: Whilst slinging a palleted water bag (load), a third-party contract worker who was assisting in the operation fell approximately 3 metres from the quayside into the water

item.title: 16/20: Lightning Conductor Fell – Dropped Object Near Miss
item.description: A lightning conductor mounted on top of a service crane came free from its mounting and dropped 75 metres

item.title: 15/20: Positive observation: Installation of disinfection tunnels
item.description: One of our Members has installed a disinfecting tunnel providing an additional control measure in the fight against the spread of COVID-19 and other diseases.

item.title: 15/20: Positive observation: Plexiglass shields installed in company shared vehicles
item.description: Following vehicle cleaning and disinfection protocol an additional initiative to protect drivers and passengers from COVID-19 during the pandemic is the installation of protective plexiglass shields in all company shared vehicles.

item.title: 15/20: COVID-19: Positive observation – maintaining social distancing during toolbox talks and meetings
item.description: The local mooring department of a contractor member has enforced strict physical distancing in external areas for toolbox talks (TBT) and other operational meetings.

item.title: 15/20: Ignited hand sanitiser
item.description: A man had his hands burnt when alcohol-based hand sanitiser caught fire.

item.title: 14/20: Lifting operations: Wire hoist rope failure
14/20: Fire in engine room and subsequent collision with structure on transport barge
item.description: During the tow of a structure to location, a fire occurred in the engine room of the tow tug. This led to a blackout resulting in a collision with the structure on the transport barge.

item.title: 14/20: LTI: Worker lost his thumb
item.description: During drilling operations, a worker got his thumb caught under a part of a drill being lowered into position, resulting in the amputation of the thumb just above the knuckle.

item.title: 14/20: LTI: Near miss: Dropped clump weight
item.description: A clump weight fell approximately 30 m to deck and landed around a metre from where a rigger was working

item.title: 14/20: Vessel gangway rolled off platform tower and fell to the quayside in high wind
item.description: During stormy weather, there were sudden and violent gusts of wind of greater than 50 knots, resulting in a vessel alongside being pushed off the quay. This resulted in the gangway rolling off the platform tower and falling approximately 5.2m to the quay. The vessel’s side of the gangway remained attached to the vessel. There was no-one nearby at the time; no-one was harmed; however, the incident had the potential to cause fatal injury.

item.title: 13/20: Recent UK MAIB investigations (shifting of cargo and loss of cargo)
item.description: An agitator in a mud tank started up when an employee of a third-party contractor working in the tank was in the way. He was hit by the agitator paddle in his lower back and fell to the tank floor.

item.title: 13/20: Grounding of ro-ro freight vessel Seatruck Performance

item.title: 13/20: Vessel flooding incident

item.title: 09/20: Potential for diver injury operating a hand-held torque wrench

item.title: 12/20: Chain hoist failure resulting in a serious near miss

item.title: 12/20: Worker fell from height and suffered life changing injuries

item.title: 12/20: Near miss: Engine room hatch left open without barriers
item.description: During routine maintenance, it was reported that the engine room hatch was left open with no physical barriers around, creating the potential for serious injury if distracted persons were to fall down the hatches.

item.title: 12/20: Agitator started moving during mud tank cleaning – leading to injury
item.description: An agitator in a mud tank started up when an employee of a third-party contractor working in the tank was in the way. He was hit by the agitator paddle in his lower back and fell to the tank floor.

item.title: 11/20: COVID-19 update
item.description: For the latest information and advice on the COVID-19 outbreak, including an overview of countries with confirmed cases and current assessments of risk, please browse to the World Health Organisation’s Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) outbreak webpage https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019.

item.title: 10/20: Dropped load and failed chain

item.title: 10/20: Lifting operation resulting in dropped objects from flexible intermediate bulk container

item.title: 10/20: Marine Safety Forum: Two incidents relating to fast rescue craft
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has published two recent Safety Alerts relating to Fast Rescue Craft (FRCs). In the first, an FRC capsized during launch. The second covers launching conditions for Fast Rescue Craft.

item.title: 10/20: Trencher angle inadvertently altered

item.title: 10/20: Damage and engine room flooding following contact by tugboat

item.description: A crew member suffered a fracture to the right-hand ring finger whilst arranging 200l oil drums

item.title: 09/20: High potential LTI: Rigger ear injury
item.description: A crew member suffered a serious ear injury whilst removing some temporary rigging suspended from a crane gantry walkway. The incident could have been much more serious; the potential was for a critical injury or fatality.

item.title: 09/20: Near miss: Failure of work procedures during hot work at height
item.description: A crew member suffered a serious ear injury whilst removing some temporary rigging suspended from a crane gantry walkway. The incident could have been much more serious; the potential was for a critical injury or fatality.

item.title: 08/20: Joint statement IMO-WHO on the response to the COVID-19 outbreak
item.description: The Director-General of WHO (the World Health Organisation) and the Secretary-General of IMO (the International Maritime Organization) have jointly issued the attached statement Circular Letter No.4204/Add.2 to assist States in ensuring that health measures are implemented in ways that minimize unnecessary interference with international traffic and trade.

item.title: 08/20: Impact of coronavirus disease (COVID-19) outbreak on Singapore-registered ships
item.description: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) has issued Shipping Circular No. 3 of 2020 relating to the impact of COVID-19 on Singapore-registered ships

item.title: 08/20: Statement on COVID-19 from UAE ministry of foreign affairs and international cooperation
item.description: The United Arab Emirates Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation issued a statement on the 24th February 2020 detailing a travel ban to Iran and Thailand following recent concerns on the new coronavirus, COVID-19, outbreaks in these countries

item.title: 07/20: High potential dropped objects from wind turbine Nacelle crane

item.title: 07/20: High potential dropped object – chains

item.description: Here are two recent prosecutions brought by the UK Health and Safety Executive, both relating to inappropriate working arrangements with live power.

item.description: This was a high potential near miss dropped object incident in which a crane boom bumper stop fell onto the crane cab. No personnel were injured; however, there was potential for serious or fatal injury.

item.description: This was a high potential near miss dropped object incident in which a crane boom bumper stop fell onto the crane cab. No personnel were injured; however, there was potential for serious or fatal injury.

item.title: 03/20: Near miss during helicopter operations
item.description: During helicopter flight boarding, a member of the crew crossed a hard barrier (stairway access chain) with a restriction sign and approached the flight deck from the aft stairway while boarding activities were ongoing on the forward side.

item.title: 03/20: Explosion and fire on-board the chemical tanker Stolt Groenland
item.description: During helicopter flight boarding, a member of the crew crossed a hard barrier (stairway access chain) with a restriction sign and approached the flight deck from the aft stairway while boarding activities were ongoing on the forward side.

item.title: 03/20: Worker fell into sea from gangway and drowned
item.description: The Singapore Tripartite Alliance for Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) has published Accident Notification 1920060 relating to a fatal fall from a gangway. This incident is still under investigation.

item.title: 03/20: MAIB: fatal man overboard incident whilst boarding tug
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published Accident Investigation Report 15/2019 into a fatality whereby a man fell overboard whilst boarding a tug at an oil terminal at Birkenhead, England

item.title: 03/20: Poor condition of on-board equipment
item.description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published Accident Investigation Report 15/2019 into a fatality whereby a man fell overboard whilst boarding a tug at an oil terminal at Birkenhead, England

item.title: 02/20: Crew member fainted after working in water ballast tank
item.description: A crew member felt faint and subsequently collapsed after working in a confined space

item.title: 02/20: Failure of life raft securing strap
item.description: A life raft from the starboard forward life raft station made an unplanned deployment into the sea

item.title: 02/20: LTI: Step into open deck hatch causes fall
item.description: During personnel transfer operations on an offshore renewables crew transfer vessel (CTV), a deckhand stepped backwards into an open hatch and fell, resulting in an injury.

item.title: 02/20: There’s something in my eye!
item.description: After shift, a member of the crew took a shower and felt that there was something in his eye. The next day he asked for help to remove it, but without success. He had to leave the vessel at the next port to have the debris removed.

item.title: 02/20: Water ingress during tropical storm
item.description: A vessel took on a significant amount of rainwater on the upper tween deck during an intense tropical storm

item.title: 30/19: Diver trapped by anchor chain
item.description: During diving operations to locate a pipeline end manifold (PLEM) near a single point mooring (SPM), a diver was trapped by an anchor chain.

item.title: 30/19: Failed shackle on vessel life raft
item.description: There was a failure of two stainless steel “D” shackles forming part of a life raft hydrostatic release assembly on a vessel.

item.title: 30/19: Uncontrolled movement of retractable gangway
item.description: During lifting up and securing of a vessel’s retractable gangway, the spring latch of the lifting device disconnected causing an uncontrolled release of the holding wire, and the gangway fell.

item.title: 30/19: Exploding television recovered from sea
item.description: One morning the crew of a workboat noticed an old television set floating in the sea near their work area. They decided to take it on-board in order to prevent it from potentially causing damage to a passing yacht or fishing boat.

item.title: 30/19: Unknown floating objects in 500m safety zone
item.description: Several unknown floating objects were identified in the 500m safety zone of an installation.

item.title: 30/19: Vessel hit and destroyed fender
item.description: A vessel collided with the quay, destroying the fenders.

item.title: 30/19: Improper use of heaving line
item.description: During a mooring operation, vessel crew were found to be using a 4 ton shackle attached to a heaving line (instead of proper “monkey fist”).

item.title: 28/19: Man overboard – Fall from a pilot ladder
item.description: While boarding a vessel via pilot ladder from a service boat, an IT service technician lost his footing and fell from the second step of the pilot ladder into the sea

item.title: 28/19: High potential incident – Man injured while falling overboard (MOB)
item.description: Whilst descending stairs to a boat-landing area on an offshore platform, a sub-contracted employee of one of our members tripped on a 2-inch discharge hose that had been laid across the base of a stairway.

item.title: 28/19: Unsafe boarding during unmooring operation
item.description: A vessel was departing from port when crew found it necessary to remove the mooring lines from the shoreside bollards with no safe un-boarding/boarding arrangements in place – instead clambering over the side

item.title: 28/19: Raising awareness on safety barriers such as railings and gratings
item.description: The Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB) of Singapore has released Safety Flyer 2019/02 entitled The importance of ensuring proper inspection and maintenance regime.

item.title: 28/19: Welder at work injured during close SIMOPS
item.description: A welder was hit and slightly injured by a lashing wire during lashing operations being conducted close by.

item.title: 29/19: Important safety notice to users of certain Crosby shackle products
item.description: Crosby has prepared an Important Safety Notice for some specific Crosby 7/8″ 6.5t shackles.

item.title: 27/19: High potential near miss: Guide cone funnel dropped
item.description: An umbilical termination head (UTH) guide cone funnel fell from its sleeve connected to the UTH body. The UTH was the 2nd end of the umbilical. It had been lifted over the vertical lay system (VLS) tower and was being prepared for deployment when the incident occurred. The UTH guide cone funnel weighed approx. 500kg and fell more than 4m towards the moonpool doors.

item.title: 27/19: Main ROV lift wire umbilical and bullet parted
item.description: An ROV vessel was engaged in subsea operation undertaking routine inspection, repair and maintenance (IRM) work.

item.title: 27/19: Cabling in ROV hanger inadvertently severed by the ROV launch and recovery frame
item.description: An ROV vessel was engaged in subsea operation undertaking routine inspection, repair and maintenance (IRM) work.

item.title: 27/19: Crush injury to hand while attempting to secure crane hook
item.description: While attempting to secure a crane hook to the deck handrail with a polypropylene rope, a rigger’s right hand was caught between the hook shank and the handrail.

item.title: 27/19: Hand injury during lift operations
item.description: During a mechanical lifting operation using a mobile crane, the crane was required to move and set up at a new location. The crane outrigger stabiliser pads (1.2T x 4) used to distribute the load from the outriggers were repositioned one at a time using a counterbalance forklift truck (FLT) and placed onto timber blocks to allow the removal of the forks.

item.title: 27/19: Finger trapped and injured whilst moving hatch covers
item.description: An AB sustained a serious finger injury when his finger was trapped while attempting to secure a forecastle hatch whilst securing the area following a mooring operation.

item.title: 26/19: Grounding of bulk carrier Kuzma Minin at Falmouth

item.title: 26/19: Use of surge protected devices on-board vessels

item.title: 26/19: Petzl Pixa lights as potential dropped objects
item.description: A member has noted that certain headlamps supplied for use with certain helmets, as used extensively for working at height in the offshore renewables sector, could come loose and fall.

item.title: 26/19: Snake on-board vessel
item.description: During a safety walk round, it was observed that a snake was on top of the anchor winch while vessel was at anchor near a port.

item.title: 26/19: Near miss: emergency stop pressed accidentally
item.description: During DP operations a vessel lost its Port azimuth thruster.

item.title: 25/19: Battery fire with subsequent gas explosion: Warning about lithium-ion power following ferry fire
item.description: The Norwegian Maritime Authority or Sjofartsdirektoratet has published an alert concerning a small fire that erupted in the battery room onboard the MF Ytterøyningen passenger ferry.

item.title: 25/19: Lithium batteries: Fire following the failure of a helicopter start power unit
item.description: The vessel fire alarm panel indicated an activated smoke detector in the Heli admin office. Upon investigation, crew found the Heli admin office to be filled with smoke; they proceeded to raise the alarm immediately and inform the Bridge.

item.title: 25/19: Fire hazard posed by personal electronic devices
item.description: A fire incident occurred in a seafarer’s cabin due to a faulty mobile phone charger. The charger was left plugged in while unattended and an electrical short circuit ignited some paper on a desk.

item.title: 25/19: Near Miss: Fire blanket caught fire during third-party hot work
item.description: While conducting a fire watch round on a vessel in port, a 2nd mate noticed that a fire blanket on the midships fire hose box had caught fire. He immediately reported this to the Bridge and used an extinguisher to put the fire out.

item.title: 25/19: Ruptured acetylene hose: Fire
item.description: A subcontractor was preparing to use an oxy-acetylene torch on the back deck of a vessel. On lighting the torch, a ‘pop’ sound was heard, and a small fire was observed from a rupture of the acetylene hose just ahead of the flash-back arrestor.

item.title: 24/19: Update to SF 11/19: Fatality and multiple injuries – flash fire onboard pipe-lay barge
item.description: This Safety Flash comprises an update on the flash fire which occurred onboard a pipe-lay barge earlier in 2019, and includes our members’ findings on the causes of the incident, and lessons learned.

item.title: 23/19: For want of a watchman, the ship was lost
item.description: A Great Lakes bulk carrier laid up for the winter suffering a catastrophic fire that caused major cosmetic, machinery, and structural damage

item.title: 23/19: UK HSE Investigation into Offshore Gas Explosion
item.description: The UK HSE has fined Marathon Oil UK LLC (Marathon) £1,160,000 following an investigation into a high-pressure gas release on the Brae Alpha offshore platform on 26 December 2015.

item.description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has published Safety Alert 11-17 relating to vessel stability and watertight integrity.

item.description: During a vessel inspection, plastic water bottles were discovered being reused to store diesel on board a fast rescue craft (FRC).
