item.title: 28/17: Finger injury: What happens when you DON’T use the right tool for the right job
item.description: A crewman attempted to remove the impeller from a fire pump using a hammer and punching rod. While he was hammering, a steel splinter of the punching rod (3-4 mm) chipped off and punctured his right hand.

item.title: 28/17: Two yard-based fatal road traffic accidents (UK HSE)
item.description: A crewman attempted to remove the impeller from a fire pump using a hammer and punching rod. While he was hammering, a steel splinter of the punching rod (3-4 mm) chipped off and punctured his right hand.

item.title: 29/17: Loss of tow and subsequent foundering of two vessels
item.description: The Danish Maritime Accident Investigation Board (DMAIB) published a Marine accident report on Maersk Battler’s loss of tow and the foundering of Maersk Searcher and Maersk Shipper in the Bay of Biscay on the night between 21 and 22 December 2016.

item.title: 27/17: Laptop battery fire
item.description: A laptop battery exploded and caught fire.

item.description: Seahealth.dk has kindly shared this safety alert with IMCA

item.title: 27/17: High potential dropped object near miss: Steel ferrule failure

item.title: 27/17: A structural failure leads to uncontrolled motion of a ‘Billy Pugh’ basket and injuries to crew
item.description: The United States Bureau of Safety & Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has issued a bulletin about an incident in which a ‘Billy Pugh’ basket was subject to uncontrolled motion leading to three crew being injured.

item.title: 27/17: Safety alert regarding the product ‘Eurogrit’: Asbestos contamination

item.description: A product-safety retrofit notice was issued by ADAMS Armaturen GmbH on 23 December 2016 and this has been recently highlighted by the International Association of Oil & Gas Producers (IOGP).

item.description: The UK Health & Safety Executive (HSE) has issued a safety bulletin regarding the safety features of the Siemens Maxum Edition II gas chromatograph (GC), following an incident involving one of these instruments, in which an instrument technician was injured as a result of an explosion.

item.title: 26/17: Loss of sight in right eye: Misdiagnosis of illness

item.title: 26/17: High potential dropped object near miss: Object fell from cargo
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) reports an incident in which a piece of grating weighing 17kg fell from a load.

item.title: 26/17: Pin from crane block sheave guard fell 25 m
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) reports an incident in which a piece of grating weighing 17kg fell from a load.

item.title: 26/17: Stored energy near miss: Person nearly hit by equipment caught during light daughtercraft operations
item.description: A stand-by diver on a light daughtercraft (LDC) was nearly hit by a flying block and tackle, which was thrown towards him by an unplanned release of tension during mooring operations

item.title: 26/17: UK HSE: Worker loses fingers in crush injury during lifting operations

item.title: 25/17: Fatality: Crew member crushed between TMS and snubber ring

item.title: 24/17: Lost time injury (LTI): Loose grating fell from crane, a man fell through and was injured
item.description: A crane operator stepped on a loose piece of grating on the crane walkway. The grating fell 18 m to deck below, damaging some stairs. The crane operator fell 4.5 m through the open grating, and suffered a fractured left leg.

item.title: 24/17: Near miss – Grating dislodged and fell, leading to crewman slipping
item.description: During flow-line installation work on an oil platform, a section of plastic grating became dislodged as a crewman stepped on it.

item.title: 24/17: Flooding in steering gear compartment
item.description: During flow-line installation work on an oil platform, a section of plastic grating became dislodged as a crewman stepped on it.

item.title: 24/17: Small boat deployment near miss incident
item.description: A vessel was carrying out a monthly rescue boat drill when, as a result of procedures not being followed, there was a sudden and unplanned deployment of the boat into the sea.

item.title: 24/17: Fatality: Overpressure of an explosion-proof enclosure
item.description: The International Association of Oil & Gas Producers (IOGP) has published an alert regarding an incident in which an engineer was fatally injured.

item.title: 23/17: Property damage: Platform supply vessel collided with legs of jack-up rig
item.description: A Platform Supply Vessel (PSV) collided with the legs of a jack-up drilling rig, causing some damage to the PSV.

item.title: 23/17: Two near misses: Loads fell from height to deck
item.description: During two recent lifting operations, loads fell from height to the deck.

item.title: 23/17: Failure of pipework in fuel tanks

item.title: 23/17: Crewman got cement dust in his eyes

item.title: 22/17: Worker trapped and injured by reversing vehicle

item.title: 22/17: Worker was injured by a forklift truck
item.description: A UK company was fined after prosecution by the Health and Safety Executive (HSE).

item.title: 22/17: Worker crushed by dropped/falling object
item.description: A UK company was fined after prosecution by the Health and Safety Executive (HSE).

item.title: 21/17: Dropped object near miss – hammer dropped from scaffolding

item.description: Step Change UK reports a fatal incident which occurred during the unpacking of heavy electrical equipment on an offshore production platform.

item.title: 20/17: Power loss within dive control

item.title: 20/17: Incorrect pressure gauge on high pressure supply line

item.title: 20/17: Oxygen and acetylene hose caught fire
item.description: On investigating the source of smoke and flames that were noticed near their work location, workers discovered some oxygen and acetylene hoses on fire.

item.title: 20/17 High potential near miss: failure of valve on gas bottle
item.description: High potential near miss: failure of valve on gas bottle

item.title: 19/17: LTI: Injury to right wrist
item.description: Someone using a power tool suffered a serious injury to the right wrist when the drill got out of control.

item.title: 19/17: LTI: Crush injury to middle and index finger
item.description: Riggers on a vessel were moving heavy deck plates (2.45 m x 1.2 m x 5 mm, weighing 114 kg) when one of them got his hand caught, causing a crush injury.

item.title: 19/17: Two cases of hand injuries – UK HSE
item.description: IMCA members continue to report significant numbers of hand and finger injuries. Here we discuss two such incidents recently reported by the UK's Health and Safety Executive (HSE).

item.title: 19/17 Hand injury whilst using pillar drill
item.description: Hand injury whilst using pillar drill

item.title: 18/17: High potential incident: Fast rescue craft capsized

item.title: 18/17: Painter parted during small boat operations

item.title: 18/17: Near miss: Failure of subsea lifting equipment

item.description: During a routine marine inspection of a vessel it was observed that rope lines had been attached to the mooring winch control levers to facilitate ‘remote’ operation of the winches.

item.title: 17/17: Fall from height – LTI
item.description: A supervisor fell 7 metres through an upper deck hatch on a vessel alongside, suffering injuries that required surgery and physiotherapy and several months away from work.

item.title: 17/17: Fall from height during yard visit
item.description: A yard worker fell 4 m from the main deck to a mezzanine deck, suffering a compression fracture in his right ankle.

item.title: 17/17: Crewman found collapsed – Seasickness
item.description: A trainee member of the crew was found lying unconscious on the deck between two cement tanks.

item.title: 17/17: Worker fainted and was injured during tanker operations in a tropical climate
item.description: After working in a crouched position on hoses aboard a tanker, a worker stood up and subsequently fainted.

item.title: 17/17: Worker suffers hand injury
item.description: The UK Health & Safety Executive (UK HSE) reports that a company was fined after a worker suffered a serious hand injury after a machinery incident.

item.title: 17/17: Worker severely burnt following oxygen explosion
item.description: The UK HSE reports that an engineering company was fined after a worker suffered life changing injuries after an oxygen pipe exploded in front of him.

item.title: 17/17: Stored energy – Worker scalded when hot ash dropped into water
item.description: The UK HSE reports that an engineering company was fined after a worker suffered life changing injuries after an oxygen pipe exploded in front of him.

item.title: 16/17: LTI: Hand injury resulting from clothing catching on door
item.description: A heavy door closed hard on a crew member's hand, injuring his thumb

item.title: 16/17: LTI: Finger injury during pilot ladder preparation
item.description: An Ordinary Seaman was injured while rigging the pilot ladder during arrival in port.

item.title: 16/17: LTI: Crewman burnt in fire following release of flammable gas from hand rail
item.description: While drilling into a handrail, a mechanic suffered burns which required time in hospital and days away from work.

The USCG notes that “these types of incidents, involving fuel leakages contacting hot surfaces and igniting, happen too frequently and have been a focus of various marine safety organizations such as the IMO for many years.”

item.title: 16/17: Chemical spill leads to costly deck replacement
item.description: The USCG has published Marine Safety Alert 01-17 relating to hazards from chemical spills.

item.title: 16/17 LTI: Burn to hand while working in laundry
item.description: LTI: Burn to hand while working in laundry

item.title: 15/17: Equipment failure leading to crane collapse
item.description: Daily soundings of fresh water tanks on a vessel revealed that they were emptying fast – 35 tonnes over 24 hours.

item.title: 15/17: Near-miss: Fault spotted in subsea lifting wire
item.description: During diving operations at 10 msw, it was noticed that there was a slight gap in the lay of the diver launch and recovery (LARS) clump weight wire.

item.title: 15/17: High potential near-miss: Mooring rope parted
item.description: Mooring buoy rope parted while the vessel was moored.

item.title: 15/17: Collared eyebolts as lifting equipment

item.title: 15/17: Near-miss: Snagged lifting bridle
item.description: The MSF has published Safety Alert 17-03 in which lifting rigging got snagged on an open top mini basket type unit.

item.title: 14/17: Near-misses during diving operations
item.description: Two near misses have occurred during diving operations.

item.title: 14/17: Near-miss: Broken chain on self-propelled hyperbaric lifeboat (SPHL) recovery rigging
item.description: Two near misses have occurred during diving operations.

item.title: 14/17: Both anchors lost due to chain fouling
item.description: A vessel had used both anchors whilst waiting for 3 days off the coast. Both chains were fouled and could not be cleared by the vessel. External assistance was provided but owing to the weather and sea conditions, the anchors could not be cleared, and both chains had to be cut. Attempts at retrieval of the anchors from the seabed were unsuccessful.

item.title: 14/17: Engine room emergency hatch damage
item.description: The engine room emergency hatch of an anchor handling tug supply (AHTS) vessel was damaged while towing a barge

item.title: 14/17: Failure of casting: Foundation brackets for steering gear
item.description: Damage was reported to the steering gear hydraulic ram foundation brackets connecting the ram to the structure of the vessel. The foundation bracket casting failed.

item.title: 14/17: Huge leak discovered in fresh water system
item.description: Daily soundings of fresh water tanks on a vessel revealed that they were emptying fast – 35 tonnes over 24 hours.

item.title: 13/17: LTI: Finger injury sustained handling heavy shackle pin
item.description: A crew member's left index finger was nipped between the head of the shackle and the body of the shackle. This resulted in a serious injury to the index finger of the left hand.

item.title: 13/17 Person accidentally drank hazardous substance: Unmarked bottle
item.description: A third-party agent on board a vessl during port clearance formalities drank from a mineral water bottle which instead of mineral water contained a small quantity of diluted bleaching liquid.

item.title: 13/17: Drill bit snapped: Finger injury sustained
item.description: A crewman was using an electric drill to fix a broom head to a broom stick, when the drill bit snapped off, causing the drill to slip, penetrating the crew member's safety glove and slightly dislodging the nail from his thumb.

item.title: 13/17: LTI: Tugger winch incident (MSF)
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has issued Safety Alert 17-01 about an incident in which an Able Seaman's foot was crushed while operating the tugger winch.

item.title: 13/17: Fatal fall aboard the tanker Marinor
item.description: The Accident Investigation Branch of Norway (AIBN) has published incident 17-04 on the fatal fall of a seafarer on board a Norwegian registered tanker, Marinor.

item.title: 12/17: How PPE works: Fire and thermal protection
item.description: The US Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published a report of a fire on an offshore production platform in the Gulf of Mexico, resulting in burn injuries to three workers.

item.title: 12/17: Galley fire: Failure to follow stove/oven installation instructions
item.description: The United States Coastguard (USCG) has published Marine Safety Alert 02-17, relating to a fire on an offshore platform.

item.title: 12/17: Dangerous modifications found within a gas valve unit room
item.description: The USCG has issued Safety Alert 05-17 to warn of a potentially dangerous situation involving modifications within gas valve unit (GVU) rooms aboard a liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier.

item.title: 12/17: Battery fire
item.description: In the early hours of the morning during a period of adverse weather the fire alarm in the vessel battery locker was activated.

item.title: 12/17: Catastrophic fire and explosion on nearby vessel
item.description: A vessel was double-banked alongside engaged with routine maintenance jobs, when a fire broke out on a vessel transporting a petroleum product which was berthed alongside at a berth 130 m away.

item.title: 12/17: Near-miss: Fire hazard from leaking fuel supply line
item.description: A potential fire hazard was discovered, caused by a failed fuel pipe connection on the supply line to the main engines.

item.title: 11/17: Dropped object injury: Equipment shifted when it was incorrectly unsecured
item.description: On a cable laying vessel, a cable quadrant had been rigged on the bulwarks, seated in a pedestal mounting and secured via lashings on the outboard side.

item.title: 11/17: LTI as a result of a load dropped from lifting magnet
item.description: A load dropped from a permanent lifting magnet hit a person’s hand resulting in an LTI.

item.title: 11/17: Dropped object: Lay tower adjuster leg pin
item.description: The securing pin from a tiltable lay system (TLS) adjuster leg, weighing 600 kg, fell 16 m to deck.

item.title: 11/17: Near-miss: Multiple potential dropped objects discovered during loading of spooling unit
item.description: After lifting operations were completed, a platform reported that multiple potential dropped objects (total 19 items) had been identified on the spooling unit.

item.title: 11/17: High potential near-miss: Incorrectly secured overhead equipment
item.description: During operations, it was observed that the connecting shackle pins on two separate items of overhead equipment (fall arrest inertia reels) were loose and could have become detached. Had any of this equipment fallen, it could have struck someone underneath with potentially fatal consequences.

item.title: 10/17: More than a dropped object – The need for vigilance during cargo operations
item.description: UK Step Change in Safety has published a ‘Safety Moment’ describing an incident in which a car travelling along a road near a port was struck by an object.

item.title: 10/17: Unsecured cargo inside containers
item.description: UK Step Change in Safety has published a ‘Safety Moment’ describing an incident in which a car travelling along a road near a port was struck by an object.

item.title: 10/17: Damage to rescue boat during lowering

item.description: A member has asked IMCA to raise awareness amongst divers and dive supervisors of the presence of Irukandji Jellyfish in certain Australian waters.

item.title: 16/13: MSF: Hand injuries
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published two safety flashes regarding hand injuries.

item.title: 15/13: Lost time injury (LTI): Dropped object incident
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which someone sustained a serious neck injury as a result of a dropped object incident.

item.title: 15/13: Incidents involving use of scaffolding
item.description: A Member has reported a number of incidents involving the use of scaffolding.

item.title: 15/13: Fire on board and sinking of liftboat Mako
item.description: The National Transportation Safety Board of the United States (US NTSB) has published the following safety flash regarding the US-registered liftboat Mako, which caught fire while supporting oil drilling operations about 6 miles off the coast of Nigeria.

item.title: 15/13: Diving helmet: Failure of sealed pull pin
item.description: A member has reported an incident without injury in which the knob of a sealed pull pin assembly (p/n 505-110) on a Kirby Morgan diver’s helmet came apart.

item.title: 15/13: MSF: Injury – Failure of hatch holdback arrangements
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-32, regarding an incident in which a crew member was injured when there was a failure of the mechanism holding back a heavy watertight door.

item.title: 14/13: MSF: Gangway detached from vessel
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-23 regarding an incident in which the gangway platform got detached from the vessel, causing the platform and the gangway to drop approximately 0.5-1 m until it was left hanging by the securing ropes and the safety net.

item.title: 14/13: MSF: High potential near-miss during cargo operations
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-24 regarding an incident in which two crewmen narrowly escaped severe crush injuries whilst engaged in cargo back-loading operations alongside a platform.

item.title: 14/13: MSF: Bulk hose entanglement with Azi-pod propulsion unit
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-26 regarding an incident in which a hose became entangled with an Azi-pod propulsion unit.

item.title: 14/13: MSF: Injuries on mud mixers
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-27 regarding two hand injury incidents, in which crew members were injured on sharp blades on mud mixing equipment on platform supply vessels.

item.title: 14/13: MSF: Fast rescue craft unplanned descent
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-29 regarding an unplanned lowering of a fast rescue craft (FRC).

item.title: 13/13: Near-miss: Un-noticed expiry and deterioration of carbon dioxide absorbent material
item.description: A member has reported a near miss incident in which carbon dioxide absorbent material expired and deteriorated beyond usable condition. This was discovered when a saturation diver reported an acidic taste in his mouth during a lock-out.

item.title: 13/13: Bunkering hose cut by propeller
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published the following safety flash, regarding an incident in which a bunkering hose was damaged because it sank and fouled the propeller.

item.title: 13/13: MSF: Crewman injured whilst changing out crane wire
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-21, regarding an incident in which someone was injured while changing out the wire on the crane.

item.title: 13/13:Spillage of oil-based mud
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published a safety flash regarding an incident in which an amount of oil-based mud (OBM) was spilt onto the deck of a newly commissioned platform supply vessel (PSV).

item.title: 13/13: Dropped object near-miss: wind sensor
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which part of a plastic fixed unit wind sensor weighing 0.8 kg dropped 10 m to the top of the bridge roof.

item.title: 12/13: Lost time injury (LTI): Crewman injured during opening of tanks
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which someone suffered a head injury, when water escaped from a tank when it was opened.

item.title: 12/13: Incidents of failure of jet drives on wind farm service vessels
item.description: A Member has reported a number of incidents involving jet drives on wind farm service vessels.

item.title: 12/13: Wind farm service vessel in collision with wind turbine foundation
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which a wind farm service vessel collided with a turbine foundation, after failure of the vessel jet drive.

item.title: 12/13: Risks associated with pneumatic hose couplings – update
item.description: The National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority of Australia (NOPSEMA) has published an updated version of its Safety Alert 55, covering the risks of incorrectly assembled, or faulty, pressurised pneumatic (air) hose couplings.

item.title: 11/13: USCG Homeport Marine Safety Alert: Recent failures of dynamic positioning (DP) systems on MODUs
item.description: The United States Coast Guard has recently issued the attached Marine Safety Alert about recent failures of dynamic positioning systems on mobile offshore drilling units.

item.title: 12/13: Near-miss: Falling transponder on main deck
item.description: The United States Coast Guard has recently issued the attached Marine Safety Alert about recent failures of dynamic positioning systems on mobile offshore drilling units.

item.title: 10/13: High potential near-miss – Lifting equipment failure
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which there was a potentially catastrophic failure of a lifting sling.

item.title: 10/13: Loading and securing of cargo
item.description: A member has highlighted two recent occasions in which containers and vehicles were inappropriately loaded and transported with their contents unsecured, which resulted in unnecessary manual handling of cargo.

item.title: 10/13: Use of portable electrical deck equipment
item.description: A Member has highlighted some recent examples of portable electrical deck equipment being used with incorrect plugs and sockets.

item.title: 10/13: USCG: Surge protective devices onboard vessels
item.description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) published in April this year a Marine Safety Alert on surge protective devices.

item.title: 09/13: High potential near-miss: Dropped ROV/TMS leading to equipment damage
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which an ROV/TMS and an A-frame docking head fell to the deck from approximately 1 m.

item.title: 09/13: Failure of lifting equipment: Dropped ROV
item.description: A member has reported an incident during offshore lifting operations in which a sling failed, causing an ROV and TMS to drop 30 cm onto deck.

item.title: 09/13: Improper securing of cargo
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-14 regarding an incident in which incorrectly stowed cargo toppled over due to the vessel’s motion on encountering unexpected adverse weather conditions.

item.title: 09/13: Generator fire incident
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which there was a small fire onboard an offshore vessel.

item.title: 09/13: NOPSEMA: Increase in dropped object events
item.description: The Australian National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority (NOPSEMA) has identified a concerning increase in dropped object events on mobile offshore drilling units (MODUs) in the first quarter of 2013.

item.title: 08/13: Substandard nitrogen quads delivered to shipyard
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which two nitrogen quads were delivered in very poor condition to a vessel in a shipyard.

item.title: 08/13: Small boat cradle collapsed during poor weather conditions
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which a zodiac inflatable boat was dropped onto deck.

item.title: 08/13: Crane wire parting
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-11 regarding the parting of a crane wire on an offshore vessel.

item.title: 08/13: Crewman injured – no control of work
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-15 regarding an incident in which someone was struck on face and arm by debris under pressure, resulting in hospitalisation to remove particles from under their skin.

item.title: 08/13: Fire caused by hot work
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which a small fire was caused by hot work taking place on the deck above.

item.title: 08/13: Counterfeit portable fire extinguishers
item.description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) published a report regarding counterfeit portable fire extinguishers.

item.title: 07/13: Dropped object injury
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-10 covering an incident in which a crew member was injured when a trolley and chain hoist came off the lifting beam.

item.title: 07/13: Gangway safety: A review of recent incidents and near-misses involving vessel gangways
item.description: The Marine Safety Forum has published safety flash 13-09 reviewing a number of incidents and near misses reported by base staff involving vessel gangways.

item.title: 07/13: Lost time injury (LTI): Serious foot injury
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a rope access technician suffered a serious injury to one of his toes, leading to partial amputation.

item.title: 07/13: Near-miss: Failure of gas quad fitting
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which there was a potentially catastrophic failure of a high pressure fitting on a gas quad.

item.title: 07/13: Lost time injury (LTI): Fall from height
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a crewman suffered an injury during a fall from height.

item.title: 07/13: Risk associated with pneumatic hose couplings
item.description: The National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority of Australia (NOPSEMA) has published the following safety alert covering the risks of incorrectly assembled or faulty pressurised pneumatic (air) hose couplings.

item.title: 06/13: Crew transfer vessel trapped under a boat landing
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a crew transfer vessel became trapped when the bottom section of a boat landing fixed to an offshore accommodation vessel gave way.

item.title: 06/13: Loss of ROV after umbilical termination failure and damage to ROV during recovery
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which there was an ROV umbilical termination failure, loss of ROV and subsequent damage to the ROV during emergency recovery from the seabed.

item.title: 06/13: Near-miss: Dropped object – falling camera
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which the mounting for a fixed camera gave way allowing the camera, weighing 25kg, to fall 4 metres.

item.title: 06/13: Near-miss: Dropped objects during lifting operations
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which pieces of angle bar slipped out of slings and fell into the sea.

item.title: 06/13: Failure of connector on marine riser
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which pieces of angle bar slipped out of slings and fell into the sea.

item.title: 05/13: Explosion causing fatal injury during maintenance of Metocean buoy
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a crewman was fatally injured during the recovery and maintenance of a metocean buoy, after it had been in use in-sea for a period of around two years.

item.title: 05/13: Battery damage caused by charger failure
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a crewman was fatally injured during the recovery and maintenance of a metocean buoy, after it had been in use in-sea for a period of around two years.

item.title: 05/13: Near-miss: Exposed live electrical cable
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a live electrical cable was found exposed.

item.title: 05/13: Finger and hand injuries
item.description: A member has reported two incidents in which crew suffered finger or hand injuries.

item.title: 05/13: High potential near-miss during equipment testing
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a heavy metal work table was dragged nearly a metre by a forklift truck.

item.title: 05/13: Pressure switch location for fixed fire suppression systems
item.description: The United States Coast Guard has published a report regarding an engine room fire in a vessel.

item.title: 04/13: Near-miss: Dropped handrail/gate near moonpool
item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a handrail gate was dislodged from its retaining points and fell 4.5m to the deck.

item.title: 04/13: Lost time injury (LTI): Fall from height leading to multiple fractures

item.title: 04/13: Near-miss: Scaffolding collapse
item.description: The National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority of Australia (NOPSEMA) has published a report regarding an incident in which a vertical scaffolding tube (a ‘dropper’) supporting a scaffolder began to slip under his weight.

item.title: 04/13: Outbreak of salmonella and gastroenteritis on an offshore facility
item.description: The National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority of Australia (NOPSEMA) has published the following report regarding a recent outbreak of salmonella and gastroenteritis on an offshore facility which resulted in about 40 members of the workforce being directly affected and led to severe disruption of offshore operations.

item.title: 04/13: Fatal crush injury during vessel hull maintenance

item.title: 03/13: Fatality during basket transfer

item.title: 03/13: Diver emergency decompression following construction barge anchor loss during tropical storm

item.description: A member has reported an incident in which a construction derrick lay barge lost all of its bow/weather anchors during a severe tropical storm.

item.title: 08/11: Hand injury while using hydraulic impact wrench
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which a diver sustained a cut injury to his left hand palm whilst working with a hydraulic impact wrench.

item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which a diver sustained a cut injury to his left hand palm whilst working with a hydraulic impact wrench.

item.title: 08/11: Electrician received electric shock
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which an electrician received an electric shock whilst working on faulty electrical equipment.

item.title: 08/11: Fatality after capsize of workboat with eight persons onboard
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which a workboat capsized during personnel transfer, causing seven people to fall into the sea, one of whom drowned.

item.title: 07/11: Reliance on crane limits caused crane damage and dropped objects
item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which a crane was damaged and objects fell to the deck in the vicinity of personnel.

item.description: A Member has reported an incident in which someone was almost caught between a crane housing and a scaffold pipe.

item.title: 07/11: Injury: Failure of subsea HP water jetting gun
item.description: Following publication in IMCA Safety Flash 05/11 (Diver safety – high pressure water jetting), which reported an incident where an injury sustained by a diver after the subsea failure of a high pressure (HP) water jetting gun, a Member would like to draw attention to a similar earlier incident.

item.title: 07/11: Incorrect information in user manual for fixed fire-fighting system

item.title: 02/11: Kirby Morgan SL 17C partially detached from neck dam

item.title: 09/07: Pinch points on winches – hand safety
item.description: A Member has identified a potentially serious hazard on a tugger winch, temporarily installed on a vessel deck, wherein a hand could be ‘drawn in’ between the winch drum cheek plate and the winch base.
